chunks: Ibn Muskan narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, who said:

Al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام said to a man: “Make your heart a companion that you keep company with, make your knowledge a parent that you follow, make your soul an enemy that you strive against, and make your wealth like a loan that you will return.”

key_terms.تُجَاهِدُهُ: you strive against it, indicating moral struggle and self-discipline
key_terms.عِلْمَكَ: your knowledge, understood as guidance to be followed
key_terms.قَلْبَكَ: your heart, the inner faculty of awareness and moral orientation
key_terms.كَعَارِيَّةٍ: like a loaned item, something temporary that must be returned
key_terms.نَفْسَكَ: your self or nafs, the lower self that must be struggled against

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام teach a believer to relate to the heart, knowledge, the soul, and wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches disciplined self-formation through inward reflection, following knowledge, struggling against the lower self, and detachment from wealth. It presents a concise ethical program in which the believer treats the heart, knowledge, nafs, and property with deliberate moral awareness.
